newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds off but outperform Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds off but outperform Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities fell Thursday, but spreads narrowed as Treasuries fell farther, mortgage experts said.
More than $2.0 billion in new corporate debt supply dragged prices lower in both markets, although its effect was felt more directly in Treasuries, analysts said.
"Mortgages are pretty much behaving in line with Treasuries," said Arthur Frank, vice president of mortgage research at HSBC Securities Inc.
Among pass-throughs, traders said Ginnie Mae 7.0-percent coupons saw better buying than other issues.
Mortgages traded off 2/32 to 10/32 overall by late Thursday, with sellers more concentrated in higher coupons, traders said.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0-percent paper was off 6/32 at 100-17/32, yielding 118 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae issues were off 7/32 at 100-17/32, and Freddie Mac paper was down 8/32 to 100-23/32.
Five-year Treasuries were off 6/32 at 6.82 percent, and 10-year notes were off 9/32 at 6.92 percent.
